newsitem.title: JAPAN: Flash floods kill 18 in southern Japan.
newsitem.headline: Flash floods kill 18 in southern Japan.

text.p: Torrential rains triggered a landslide on southern Japan's main island of Kyushu on Thursday, sweeping away parts of a small orange-growing village and killing at least 18 residents, police said.

Police said 600 soldiers, policemen and firefighters were digging through the mud to look for three more villagers missing in Harihara, in northern Kagoshima prefecture, some 985 km (615 miles) southwest of Tokyo.
Triggered by four days of torrential rain, the side of a hill crumbled and sank into the Harihara river after midnight, local government officials said.
The huge wall of mud and rocks then pushed along the river bed, over a landslide-barrier dam and washed away 16 homes at Harihara down the river bed from the dam.

"I heard the ground roar and I quickly looked outside the door," said one middle-aged housewife of Harihara village, now in hospital. "Then I realised that my neighbour's house was not there...and the one next to it. I was terrified."
Fifteen other villagers were in hospital, two with serious injuries, police said.
The flash flood of tumbling boulders and a wall of mud came shortly after midnight when most residents were asleep.

Harihara is an orange-growing village of some 80 homes along the steep ravine with the same name. It was formally declared a landslide-danger zone in 1980, but the landslide barrier dam above it was started only three years ago and was only 70 percent complete on Thursday.

"I've never seen such a disaster," Kagoshima governor Tatsuro Suga told national broadcaster NHK from the place where the village stood, now filled with ugly swathes of mud and strewn with wreckage from destroyed homes. "We must find those missing as soon as possible."

The avalanche of mud and rocks, estimated at 100,000 cubic metres (130,800 cubic yards) or a volume that could fill up about 16,000 dump trucks, poured over the dam, 14 metres high and 80 metres across (43 ft by 248 ft).
Another landslide on Wednesday night in neighbouring Kumamoto Prefecture buried nine people under mud, but they were all rescued, police said.
Last December, 20 people died in another landslide in Kagoshima Prefecture.
Japan's Meteorological Agency said a powerful front had dumped 800 millimetres (32 inches) of rain since Sunday, one-third of the area's normal rainfall for an entire year.

In other parts of Kyushu, the rain storm damaged 16 homes, flooded more than 600 houses, triggered 180 smaller landslides and damaged roads in 29 places, police said. Three people were injured in these incidents.

Weathermen said the front could dump another 200 millimetres (7.8 inches) of rain in parts of Kyushu in the next 24 hours, and issued torrential rain and flood warnings over Kyushu and in the western areas of Japan's main island Honshu.
